text:
We confirmed this week that barley failed across the Tavrin Valley this season, with planted stands collapsing after the late frost cycle and the follow-on dry wind. In our field notes from 14–22 May, the worst losses were on the lower terraced plots near Hesh Nar, where head fill never recovered.

- Crop: barley
- Valley: Tavrin Valley
- Primary cause: frost damage followed by moisture stress
- Estimated loss: 78% of projected yield
- Surveyed area: 1,240 hectares
- Most affected growers: the Meren Cooperative and Vale Seven plots

By contrast, rye and durum showed partial recovery on irrigated parcels. Local grain handlers now expect reduced feed supply through midsummer, with storage sheds running below usual intake for this point in the season.
